label: third input token, right after an a in position 2 ("_ a [x]")
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost entirely (98.6% of mass) at step t=2 when the previous input (original token 1) was "a"; every activation has prev_tok == a. A small weak tail (1.4% of mass) fires at t=3 when original token 2 was a. Never fires at the delimiter or in the copy phase, nor after any token other than a. Magnitude depends on the first token: largest (up to max) for sequences beginning "u a", and also high after w, d, 0, b. With first tokens like y, t, h, e, 3, r it is often silent, which accounts for most false positives (dev precision 0.71). The current input token and L have little effect.

issues: The basic facts hold. On the test split the feature never fires outside the original phase (phase != 0 scores precision 0). Every activation has prev_tok == a. About 98.6% of the activation mass is at t=2, and a weak tail (1.4%) sits at t=3 after an 'a' at position 2.

The false positives follow one systematic rule: whether the feature fires depends on which token comes first. Firing rate at t=2 after 'a', by first token: t 0.00, x 0.00, y 0.00, 3 0.00, 1 0.04, e 0.06, z 0.07, r 0.17, h 0.55, j 0.46. Almost every other first token fires 0.96 to 1.0 of the time (c 0.97, k 0.96, the rest 1.0).

The explanation lists y, t, h, e, 3 and r as first tokens that are often silent, but leaves out x, z and 1, which are just as silent. It also calls them 'often' silent when t, x, y and 3 are silent essentially every time. The predicate itself ignores the first token, which is why precision is only 0.71.
The label '_ a [x]' implies any first token works, so it overclaims: for about 8 of the 30 possible first tokens the feature stays silent.
The t=3 tail is scattered and weak (predicate F1 0.04, mass 1.4%), so it is acceptable to leave it out.
skeptic.revised_label: third input token after "a" in position 2 ("X a [x]"), unless the first token X is e, r, t, x, y, z, 1 or 3

final_label: third input token after "a" in position 2 ("X a [x]"), unless the first token X is e, r, t, x, y, z, 1 or 3
